cases: ordinary string literal inside a function body changes

func value() -> String { "old" }
func value() -> String { "new" }
interpolated string content changes without a declaration change

func value(_ name: String) -> String { "hello \(name)" }
func value(_ name: String) -> String { "welcome \(name)" }

func value() -> String { #"old \#(1)"# }
func value() -> String { #"new \#(1)"# }
extended raw string delimiter and content remain implementation-only

func value() -> String { ##"old \##(1)"## }
func value() -> String { ##"new \##(1)"## }
declaration-looking words in a string do not affect the surface

func value() -> String { "class Fake { var x = 1 }" }
func value() -> String { "actor Fake { let y = 2 }" }
nested block comments containing declaration tokens stay ignored

func value() -> Int { /* outer /* struct Fake {} */ old */ 1 }
func value() -> Int { /* outer /* class Fake {} */ new */ 2 }
line comments with declaration-looking text remain implementation-only

func value() -> Int { 1 } // var fake = 1
func value() -> Int { 2 } // class fake {}
comment-only edits remain hot-reloadable under the legacy compatibility contract

func value() -> Int { 1 /* old */ }
func value() -> Int { 1 /* new */ }

actor Worker { func value() -> Int { 1 } }
actor Worker { func value() -> Int { 2 } }
generic method body changes without signature changes

struct Box<T> { func map<U>(_ f: (T) -> U) -> U { fatalError("a") } }
struct Box<T> { func map<U>(_ f: (T) -> U) -> U { fatalError("b") } }
initializer body changes without signature changes

struct Item { let x: Int; init(x: Int) { self.x = x } }
struct Item { let x: Int; init(x: Int) { self.x = max(0, x) } }
